title: Intermittent attention precision regression during quantized-kernel handshake causing token corruption in long prefill
creator: Sophia Nguyen
description: Symptoms observed after introducing a runtime optimization that performs an on-the-fly kernel handshake (switch) between FP16 and int8-friendly kernels during long prefill windows. In a subset of long-prefill requests (>1024 tokens) the model output showed subtle token corruption (wrong punctuation, occasional token duplication) that only manifests after decode begins. The corruption is nondeterministic at high concurrency and correlates with GPU kernel switches and boundary KV-cache writes. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigations, and a safe rollout plan.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a local serving replica with runtime-1.20+quant-handshake enabled
Load a 8B-class model with int8 quantization profile applied
Send a prefill request containing ~1200 tokens of context that exercises long attention spans
Immediately follow with streaming decode to generate ~50 tokens at concurrency 8+
Observe output tokens for duplication, punctuation drift, or subtle token substitutions across runs
observed_behavior: Intermittent token-level corruption that appears only when the runtime switches kernel implementations mid-request; reproduces ~5-15% of test runs under stress. Failure modes: repeated token subsequences, occasional token ID mismatch leading to punctuation changes, and rare off-by-one in attention scores when kernel switch occurs during KV-cache flushes.
expected_behavior: No change in decoded tokens compared to baseline FP16 path; deterministic outputs for identical seeds and inputs regardless of kernel selection or concurrency.
investigation_notes: 2025-02-19: Initial report from e2e test harness (ci/long-prefill-stability) — failing 6/100 runs.
2025-02-20: Reproduced locally with binary build including handshake enabled; added logging around kernel switch points.
2025-02-21: Narrowed window to kernel-switch during prefill->decode boundary; hypothesis: stale KV-cache pointers or truncated attention key/value tensors when using fused kernel path.
2025-02-22: Added per-layer checksum (float32 sum reduction) before and after kernel switch; checksum mismatch appears on ~10% runs and correlates with corruption.
2025-02-24: Ported checksum to run on CPU copy path to validate it isn't a host->device DMA ordering bug — mismatch persists only when handshake is enabled.
2025-02-26: Experimented with forced cudaDeviceSynchronize() at handshake; failure rate dropped to 0/200 runs but latency regressed ~8%.

2025-02-28: Found race in handshake state machine: kernel selection completed and returned while asynchronous KV writes from prefill were still pending; subsequent kernel assumed ownership of the KV buffer and performed in-place quantization overwriting bytes still being produced by prefill.
2025-03-01: Confirmed root cause by instrumenting event timestamps and stream fences; reproduced deterministic corruption by removing a stream fence in a controlled test harness.
root_cause: A concurrency race in the kernel-handshake path: the quantized-kernel selection path did not consistently wait for the prefill write stream to complete before in-place tensor transformations (quantize/pack). This allowed overlapping writes and in-place modifications to the KV cache, producing numerical drift and token corruption during decode. The issue is exacerbated by aggressive fusion of attention kernels and smaller memory alignment changes introduced by the int8 packer.
short_term_mitigation: Disable kernel-handshake (fallback to FP16 kernel) for models with prefill length >1024 via rollout flag (config: handshake.prefill_threshold_tokens)
Add conservative stream fences around KV-cache writes during prefill for affected models in Dedicated customers with high SLAs
Deploy a health-check in the console to detect increased token-level regression for customers on runtime-1.20 and automatically toggle handshake off for impacted customer workloads
long_term_fix: Refactor handshake state machine to use explicit CUDA events and ensure producer-consumer ordering across streams
Introduce copy-then-quantize path for overlapping windows rather than in-place packing when prefill and handshake overlap
Extend CI stress tests with seeded long-prefill reproducer and include checksum asserts in hardware-in-loop runs
Add deterministic integration test that runs kernel-switch permutations under high concurrency to prevent regressions
test_plan: Add unit test covering handshake ordering semantics (simulate async writes and quantize packer)
Add integration test to nightly that sends 10k long-prefill requests across model variants and asserts checksums and decoded tokens match baseline
Run dedicated canary on staging with disabled handshake for top 20% long-prefill customers then enable with fences to validate correctness and latency impact
Benchmark latency/cost before/after fixes to provide guidance for rollout gating thresholds
